slots.enablecomp-response-fixture/title: The first release must join intake, ownership, integration, evidence, and change
slots.enablecomp-response-fixture/row-copy-1/p: Evidence for operations: link status, access, and processing events to an auditable case history; distinguish incomplete intake, waiting decisions, technical failures, and genuine demand.
slots.enablecomp-response-fixture/row-copy-2/p: Measure completeness and first-touch rework using agreed definitions.
Clear ownership: assign a business owner, service queue, and escalation path to each case state; record decisions and reassignment reasons.
slots.enablecomp-response-fixture/row-copy-3/p: Controlled integration: use versioned interfaces and event contracts, starting with one supported integration; do not assume real-time support from every legacy interface.
slots.enablecomp-response-fixture/row-copy-4/p: Reliable intake: validate minimum information, establish a consistent case identifier, expose missing information, and preserve alternate intake routes during transition.
slots.enablecomp-response-fixture/row-copy-5/p: These are proposed requirements, not evidence of implemented capability.

Sustainable change: transfer runbooks, service ownership, release controls, and improvement routines; agree support responsibilities before first production release. One supported integration is the starting assumption; wider interface support requires validation.
slots.slide/takeaway: Five connected operating needs shape the first release and its acceptance measures.
